audience: Cline is for people who want an agent in the editor or the CLI and refuse a seat fee. The verdict says the agent is free and Apache-2.0, and you pay whatever model provider you connect. That includes a local model. If you already manage API keys, you are the audience.

It is a poor fit if you want someone else to cap the bill. The cons are blunt: API bills can pass a $20 editor subscription, and you set up keys and approvals yourself. A developer who wants one login and a known monthly price should buy that subscription instead of pretending a free agent is the same thing.
features: The Cline row is Free under Apache-2.0. Model usage is pay your API provider. There is no second paid tier hiding under a contact-sales button in our table. The pricing source is cline.bot, checked 14 October 2026.
Open source, with a CLI and an IDE extension, is the practical pro. You can point it at any provider. A local model is allowed, which is the escape hatch when you do not want a hosted key at all.

Approvals are part of the product. You watch the agent and you allow the step. That is slower than a fire-and-forget cloud agent, and it is also how you keep a free tool from rewriting a repo you did not mean to touch.
limitations: The $20 comparison in the cons is the whole pricing story. Claude Pro is $20 a month and includes Claude Code. GitHub Copilot Pro is $10 a month. If your provider invoice is already higher than those, Cline's free license is not saving you money. It is only saving you a seat.

You set up keys and approvals yourself. There is no included token credit in the table, and we will not invent one. A local model avoids the API line and adds the cost of running it, which is not a Cline price.
The rating is Depends. Depends is the honest grade for a free agent with an uncapped provider bill. The license is not a verdict that every month will be cheap.

faqs.a: The agent is free under Apache-2.0. The model is not, unless you run a local one. The table's second row is pay your API provider.

faqs.q: Can the API bill cost more than a $20 editor plan?
faqs.a: Yes. That is the cons line. Claude Pro is $20 a month and GitHub Copilot Pro is $10 a month. If your key spend is past those, the free license is not the cheaper product.

faqs.q: Can I use a local model?
faqs.a: Yes. The pros say any provider, including a local model. That removes the hosted API line. It does not add a Cline fee.
Because the software is free and the usage is not capped by Cline. Depends means use it if you will watch the key, and buy a seat with an allowance if you will not.
